subject: Draft case study: Borealis AI — performance & cost savings (review)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@borealis.ai>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@borealis.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Draft case study attached for Borealis AI — first pass

Hi Alex + Priya,

Thanks again for the time last week — it was great to map the outcomes you saw on Redwood Dedicated. I’ve attached a second-pass draft of the Borealis AI case study (borealis-case-draft-v2.docx). The doc captures:
- the architecture you used (Dedicated pool + prefix caching)
- the primary metric improvements (avg latency, cost per 1k tokens)
- the customer quote we captured during the interview

Would you mind reviewing for technical accuracy and tone? Two asks: (1) please mark any redlines directly in the doc or send back a PDF with comments, and (2) confirm the final quote we pulled from your interview — I quoted Alex: "Redwood cut our inference cost by ~42% while improving P95 latency by ~25%"; let me know if that’s okay to publish verbatim or if you prefer a softened number.

If you prefer a shared doc, here’s the live link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A2B3C4D5E6F7G8H9

Target timeline: if we can lock changes by EOD Monday 10/18 we’d aim to publish the case study week of Oct 25.

Attachments: [Attachment: borealis-case-draft-v2.docx (DOCX - 98KB)]

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Growth Marketing Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@borealis.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@borealis.ai>
Cc: Jordan Hale <juris@borealis.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft case study attached for Borealis AI — first pass

Marissa — thanks for the draft and the clear structure. I reviewed and left inline comments; I’m also returning a PDF with our redlines. High level: great framing, but two factual fixes and one ask from Legal.

Corrections:
1) The 42% cost reduction number should be 38% (that’s the normalized average across our production runs after accounting for caching). Please update the percentage and add a short parenthetical note on how it was measured ("normalized across X workloads").
2) The latency improvement is closer to 20% P95 (not 25%) — Rafael can confirm the exact window if needed.

Legal ask: please remove the sentence that references our internal per-request SLA ("we saw consistent sub-100ms for all requests") — that is sensitive. Jordan from Legal is CC’d and will confirm any required redaction.

I attached Borealis' annotated PDF (borealis-redlines.pdf) with line notes.

On the quote: you may publish a slightly softened line — "Redwood reduced our inference costs significantly while improving latency for critical endpoints" — but I’d prefer to keep the exact percentages only in the technical sidebar.

If you need a final stamp after updates, I can do a final pass on Tue 10/20.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Mercer | VP, Engineering
Borealis AI
[Attachment: borealis-redlines.pdf (PDF - 12KB)]

- I confirm the normalized cost reduction is 38% across the three benchmarked workloads (batch inference + interactive routing + reranking).
- P95 moved to 20% improvement when using the 30-day production window we agreed on.
- For the SLA redaction, I suggest: "Borealis observed materially improved tail latency on production traffic after migrating to Redwood Dedicated." That keeps the result public-friendly without exposing internal SLA numbers.
